title: Ahmed Tibi elected deputy speaker of Israel’s Knesset
html:
An Arab member of Israel’s parliament, Ahmed Tibi, the chairman of the Joint List alliance, has been elected deputy speaker of the Knesset.

Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party, will be chairman of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee, the panel said on Monday.

“This is a rightful achievement for the Joint List, which secured 11 seats” in the October 27 elections, Tibi told Al Jazeera.

He added that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir “attempted to prevent my election, but they failed despite their reckless incitement. The Joint List will be represented in all committees.”

Tibi is the leader of the Ta’al party, which is part of the Joint List.

The parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel – the Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) – made historic electoral gains in last month’s elections, securing a cumulative 19 seats in parliament.

The bloc endorsed Gadi Eisenkot after President Isaac Herzog tasked him this month with forming the next government.

Palestinian-led parties are now focused on using their increased representation to address discrimination and other issues facing their community.

Call for criminal investigation

Tibi on Sunday called for a criminal investigation into Netanyahu and his aides, accusing them of engaging in “Mafia-style conduct” after an investigative media report accused them of interference in the parliamentary elections.

According to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster, Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, contacted the police commissioner’s office before the October 27 Knesset elections, alleging that three activists from the Ra’am party in southern Israel were carrying large sums of cash and vouchers intended to sway voters.

Police relied on information from an intelligence source, who was a former employee of the prime minister’s office, to arrest the activists after raiding their homes without valid search or arrest warrants.

“No one is above the law, not even Netanyahu,” Tibi said on X, calling for the criminal investigation.

Tibi was first elected to the Israeli Knesset in 1999 and has served as deputy speaker of the Knesset between 2006 and 2022.
summary: Tibi says the appointment is a 'rightful achievement' for the Joint List.
